newsitem.title: USA: Hurricane Lili pounds central Cuba, Bahamas braced.
newsitem.headline: Hurricane Lili pounds central Cuba, Bahamas braced.

text.p: Hurricane Lili pounded central Cuba Friday with sustained 90 mph (145 kph) winds and torrential rains as the Bahamas braced for the coming storm, National Hurricane Center said.
At 0800 EDT/1200 GMT, Lili's center was at latitude 22.7, longitude 81.6 west, about 35 miles (55 km) south-southwest of Varadero, Cuba, and moving northeast at about eight 8 mph.

The storm's top winds were unlikely to decrease while it moved over land, forecasters said. Sustained winds of 92 mph with gusts up to 115 mph were measured early Friday at Cayo Largo del Sur, near the south coast of central Cuba.

A hurricane warning remained in effect for Cuba's Isle of Youth and the mainland from Camaguey province westward, and for the northwest Bahamas. A hurricane watch was in effect for the central Bahamas.
A tropical storm warning remained in effect for the Florida Keys from Key Largo to the Dry Tortugas including Florida Bay.
Forecasters said Lili was expected to remain on its current track with an increase in forward speed during the next 24 hours, putting the eye over mainland Cuba Friday and the Bahamas on Saturday.
Hurricane-force winds extended outward up to 30 miles from the center and tropical storm-force winds extended out about 140 miles.
The storm threatened to dump up to 12 inches (30 cm) of rain in its path, raising the possibility of life-threatening flash floods and mudslides in mountainous areas, forecasters said.
It also threatened storm surge flooding of three to six feet (one to two meters), particularly near and to the east of where the center crosses the coast, forecasters said.
